mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 0.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals labor market distress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth and HOUST both positive in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS growth and HOUST are positive in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost of goods sold, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in late-cycle conditions.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 5 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months and UNRATE is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.
